# Changelog

The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and the project follows
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). Pre-1.0, a feature bumps the minor
version and a fix bumps the patch version; 1.0.0 is reserved for the proof-of-concept delivery.

**Do not edit this file in a pull request.** Add a change fragment under `.changes/unreleased/`
instead (see `.changes/README.md`). The sections below are assembled from those fragments at release
time, which is why two branches in flight never conflict over a changelog entry.

<!-- new releases go here -->

## [0.1.1] - 2026-07-14

### Security

- Neutralise spreadsheet formulas in CSV exports. A cell opening with =, +, - or @ is executed by Excel and Google Sheets, and DEMO_MODE hands these exports to strangers.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-07-14

The SvelteKit proof of concept, rewritten from the original Laravel app, and the first version that
runs end to end: add a wallet, sync it from Blockfrost, categorise the transactions, read and export
the statements.

### Added

- Wallet ingestion from Blockfrost: add a wallet by address, ADA `$handle`, or a CIP-30 browser
  wallet. History is paged in the background by a BullMQ worker, and the eUTxO data is diffed into
  per-counterparty flows.
- The accounting engine: a cash-book double-entry ledger over the derived flows, producing a
  consolidated Trial Balance, Balance Sheet, and Profit and Loss statement, denominated in ADA.
  Transfers between your own wallets net out.
- Default categorisation on ingest, with a dropdown to re-categorise any transaction against the
  chart of accounts.
- An address book for naming counterparties.
- CSV export of the Trial Balance, Balance Sheet, P&L, and the full transaction register.
- Settings, for the entity name that heads every statement and export.
- A public read-only demo (`DEMO_MODE=true`): `/demo` serves the statements and their exports with no
  account, and anonymous visitors land there instead of at a login wall. Off by default, because it
  publishes the instance's books.
- Authentication via Better Auth, shared with the other Mercury apps through
  `@cardano-mercury/core`. `SINGLE_USER_MODE` (the default) lets the first sign-up claim the instance
  and then closes registration.
- A `/healthz` endpoint that checks Postgres, not just the HTTP server.
- Production images: `mercury-financials` (the app) and `mercury-financials-migrate` (a one-shot).
- `docs/deployment.md`, covering the shared-database rules, migration order, and the demo.

### Changed

- Every table this app owns is prefixed `financials_`. The Mercury apps share one Postgres, and the
  old generic names (`accounts`, `transactions`, `addresses`) sat one typo away from core's auth
  `account` table. `drizzle-kit` is fenced in with `tablesFilter` and its own migration journal.
- The shared Better Auth tables are no longer created here. They belong to `@cardano-mercury/core`,
  which owns their migrations.
- The database client and the auth instance are constructed lazily. Building them at module scope
  meant `npm run build` required a live `DATABASE_URL` and a real `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, because
  SvelteKit's postbuild step imports every server chunk.

### Removed

- The `db:push` script. `tablesFilter` does not cover sequences, so `drizzle-kit push` proposes
  dropping the _tokenomics_ migration journal and would destroy its history. Use `db:generate` and
  `db:migrate`, which only apply committed SQL.

### Fixed

- A failed sync no longer wedges a wallet permanently. BullMQ treats `add()` with an existing job id
  as a silent no-op, including for a job that already failed, so one failed sync left a dead job in
  Redis and every later Sync did nothing while reporting success.
